content.text: I have the packet; no external lookups are permitted beyond it, so I will assess directly against the rubric.

findings: Direct support for the exact claim and its stated scope: The claim is a five-part mapping table, and only three of the five entries are directly supported by the supplied citations. KEGG COMPOUND C00270 lists 'Neu5Ac' among the names of 'N-Acetylneuraminate; N-Acetylneuraminic acid', and the BRITE line 'C00270  N-Acetylneuraminic acid' corroborates the full name, supporting Neu5Ac = N-acetylneuraminic acid (though not the parenthetical gloss 'sialic acid', which appears in no supplied quote). KEGG C00140 lists 'GlcNAc' among the names of 'N-Acetyl-D-glucosamine', supporting GlcNAc = N-acetylglucosamine. The ChEBI/OLS4 record for CHEBI:28037 lists 'GalNAc' and 'D-GalNAc' as synonyms alongside 'N-acetyl-D-galactosamine', reinforced by KEGG 'C01132  N-Acetyl-D-galactosamine', supporting GalNAc = N-acetylgalactosamine. In contrast, no supplied citation states 'Man' as an abbreviation for mannose — there is no mannose reference in the packet at all — and the only fucose quote gives '6-Deoxy-L-galactose', '6-deoxy-L-galactopyranose' without stating the abbreviation 'Fuc' or even the word 'fucose' in the quoted text. Because the claim is asserted as a single tabulated set, two of its five symbol-to-name pairings are unevidenced within the packet, so the exact claim is not fully supported.

Source applicability, qualifications and conflicting evidence: The sources are appropriate in kind — KEGG COMPOUND and EMBL-EBI ChEBI/OLS4 are authoritative chemical-compound registries, retrieved over public HTTPS from canonical REST endpoints, version-pinned to 2026-09-15, and licensed for quotation (KEGG academic terms; ChEBI CC BY 4.0). However, their scope is chemical nomenclature and synonymy, not the IUPAC-condensed/glycan symbol notation named in the claim's scope, so they serve as indirect rather than on-scope authority: they confirm that certain short forms are recorded synonyms of certain compounds, not that those short forms constitute the IUPAC condensed glycan symbol set. No supplied citation contradicts any part of the claim; there is no counter-assignment of Neu5Ac, GlcNAc, GalNAc, Man or Fuc to a different monosaccharide anywhere in the packet. The submission's own limitations note flags a divergence rather than a contradiction: KEGG classifies Neu5Ac under amino sugars rather than under a 'sialic acid' label, and ChEBI frames fucose as a deoxyhexose — these are classification-vocabulary differences that neither confirm nor refute the claim's name mappings, but they do leave the 'sialic acid' parenthetical uncorroborated. One further reference (Essentials of Glycobiology, NBK579927) is pinned but unquoted and therefore carries no evidentiary weight here.

Uncertainty and limits of a documentary conclusion: This assessment compares claim text to quoted source text only; it establishes nothing about whether the skill actually returns these names when given these abbreviations. The packet itself records that the subject skill was never executed for this claim and that the required grade-critique step failed three times in the run, so there is no behavioural or performance evidence whatsoever — the 'expected_behavior' (returning the tabulated full name on input of an abbreviation) is entirely untested. Even for the three supported pairings, the evidence type is synonym co-listing in a compound registry, which shows the abbreviation is a recognised alias but does not itself verify a lookup implementation, its coverage, its handling of stereochemical qualifiers (D-/L- prefixes appear in the sources but not in the claim's names), or its behaviour on inputs outside the five listed. The two unevidenced pairings (Man, Fuc) are widely conventional in glycan notation, but conventional familiarity is not documentary support; absence of a citation here yields insufficiency, not falsity. Accordingly the correct documentary verdict is that support is incomplete rather than that the claim is wrong.

The packet states the subject skill was never executed for this claim, so the expected behaviour — returning the tabulated full name when given an abbreviation — is wholly untested here. Nothing in this assessment speaks to the skill's accuracy, coverage, error handling, determinism, or behaviour on abbreviations outside the five listed.

It cannot confirm the two unevidenced mappings. No supplied citation mentions mannose at all, and the fucose quote states only '6-Deoxy-L-galactose' / '6-deoxy-L-galactopyranose' without the token 'Fuc'. Their absence here is an evidentiary gap, not a demonstration that these mappings are incorrect; a differently constituted packet could readily resolve them.

It cannot validate the claim's scope framing. The cited sources are chemical-compound registries (KEGG COMPOUND, ChEBI via OLS4) documenting synonymy, not normative specifications of IUPAC-condensed or SNFG glycan symbol notation. Synonym co-listing shows an abbreviation is a recognised alias of a compound; it does not certify that the claim's five-symbol set is the IUPAC condensed set, nor that it is complete or exclusive.

It cannot adjudicate ancillary descriptors. The parenthetical '(sialic acid)' and the claim's implied type labels (Hexose, HexNAc, Sialic acid) are not stated in any quoted passage; the sources use different classification vocabulary (amino sugars, deoxyhexose). This divergence is left unresolved rather than decided.

Finally, quote fidelity, retrieval provenance, licence terms and version pinning are taken as supplied and were not independently re-fetched or re-verified, and the pinned-but-unquoted Essentials of Glycobiology reference contributed no evidence.
